hook.situation: You are texting someone what you are doing right now, why you did not reply, or what happened during another action.
objectives: Use V-고 있어요 for an action in progress.
Use V-는 중이에요 or N 중이에요 when you are right in the middle of something.
Use V-는 동안 to show what happens during the same time span.
hook.whyItMatters: Korean does not need a separate word like English 'am/is/are doing.' The ongoing meaning is built with endings and nouns: 공부하고 있어요, 공부하는 중이에요, 공부하는 동안. These forms make Kakao replies and daily updates much more natural.

grammarNotes.title: V-고 있다 — an action in progress
grammarNotes.func: Add -고 있다 to a verb stem to say an action is happening right now. It is the closest match to English 'be -ing' (am/is/are doing).

formTable.when: Any verb stem (vowel or consonant): drop -다, add -고 있다
formTable.ex: 먹다 → 먹고 있다 (eating), 보다 → 보고 있다 (watching)

examples.note: 지금 + -고 있어요 is the go-to pair for something happening this very moment.

examples.en: My friend is reading a book.
examples.note: Other people work the same way; just change the subject to 친구가.

examples.en: My little brother is watching a movie.
examples.note: 보다 ends in a vowel and still just takes -고 있어요 — the rule never changes.

examples.en: I was studying Korean a little while ago.
examples.note: -고 있었어요 is the past version: 'was doing.'

keyPoint.label: -고 있어요 vs. plain -아요/-어요
keyPoint.body: 먹어요 can mean 'I eat (usually)' or even 'I'll eat.' 먹고 있어요 pins it down to 'I'm eating right now.' Reach for -고 있어요 when you want to make clear the action is happening as you speak.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 있어요 runs together as [이써요], and -고 tenses to [꼬] after ㄱ, so 먹고 있어요 sounds like [먹꼬 이써요].

drill.instruction: Say what each person is doing right now with -고 있어요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English can say 'I'm liking it,' but Korean feeling/state verbs like 좋아하다, 알다, 사랑하다 don't take -고 있다 for a current state. Just use the plain present. Save -고 있다 for actions you can actually watch happening.

grammarNotes.title: V-는 중이에요 / N 중이에요 — in the middle of
grammarNotes.func: 중 means 'the middle of.' Add -는 중이에요 to a verb stem, or just 중이에요 to a noun, to say you're 'in the middle of' something right now.

formTable.when: Verb stem + -는 중이에요 (vowel or consonant stem)
formTable.ex: 먹다 → 먹는 중이에요 (in the middle of eating)

formTable.when: ㄹ-stem verb: drop ㄹ, then add -는 중이에요
formTable.ex: 만들다 → 만드는 중이에요 (in the middle of making)
회의 → 회의 중이에요 (in a meeting), 공부 → 공부 중이에요

examples.en: I'm in the middle of eating right now.
examples.note: -는 중이에요 plays up that you're partway through it, not done.
기다리다 ends in a vowel and just takes -는 중이에요.
With a noun like 공부, drop the verb and say just 'noun + 중이에요' — no 을/를.
전화 중이에요 is the set phrase for 'on the phone.'

keyPoint.label: -는 중이에요 vs. -고 있어요
keyPoint.body: Both mean 'be doing,' but -는 중이에요 means you're smack in the middle of one specific action, so it can't describe a lasting state. You can say 한국에 살고 있어요 (I'm living in Korea), but not 사는 중이에요 — 중 needs a action that starts and stops, like eating or waiting.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 먹는 → ㄱ before ㄴ turns into [ㅇ] (nasal), so 먹는 sounds like [멍는]: [멍는 중이에요].

drill.instruction: Answer '지금 뭐 해요?' saying you're right in the middle of it, with -는 중이에요 or N 중이에요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: 중 is a noun, so it needs 이에요 after it: 중이에요, not 중에요. Learners drop the 이 because it goes by fast when spoken, but the full form keeps 중 + 이에요.

grammarNotes.title: V-는 동안 — while / during
grammarNotes.func: 동안 means 'the whole time of.' Add -는 동안 to a verb stem to say 'while (someone) is doing something.' The main action happens over that same stretch of time.

formTable.when: Verb stem + -는 동안 (vowel or consonant stem)
formTable.ex: 먹다 → 먹는 동안 (while eating), 자다 → 자는 동안 (while sleeping)

formTable.when: ㄹ-stem verb: drop ㄹ, then add -는 동안
Noun + 동안 ('for / during' a stretch of time)
formTable.ex: 한 시간 → 한 시간 동안 (for one hour), 방학 → 방학 동안 (during vacation)

examples.en: While I cooked, my friend cleaned.
examples.note: Two people, same time: I cook, my friend cleans.

examples.ko: 동생이 자는 동안 저는 책을 읽었어요.
examples.romanization: dongsaengi janeun dongan jeoneun chaegeul ilgeosseoyo.
examples.en: While my little brother was sleeping, I read a book.
examples.note: 자다 → 자는 동안. The main verb (past) tells you when it all happened.

examples.en: I watched a movie while I ate.
examples.note: One person doing both at once is fine too.

examples.en: I'll study Korean during the vacation.
examples.note: With a noun like 방학, use just 'noun + 동안' for 'during / for' that time.

keyPoint.label: -는 동안 (always 는) vs. -(으)ㄹ 때
keyPoint.body: -는 동안 always keeps -는, no matter the tense, because it marks a whole stretch of time. 때 ('when') points at one moment or occasion; 동안 covers the full length. Use 동안 when one action runs the whole time another is going on.

grammarNotes.pronunciation: 먹는 동안 → 먹는 nasalizes to [멍는] (ㄱ+ㄴ → ㅇ+ㄴ), so it's [멍는 동안].

drill.instruction: Join the two halves with -는 동안 to mean 'while ___, ___.'
drill.model: 제가 자다 / 엄마가 요리하다 → 제가 자는 동안 엄마가 요리했어요.

englishSpeakerPitfall.explanation: English puts 'while' on a past verb ('while I ate'), so learners add 었 before 동안. In Korean, -는 동안 stays in the -는 form no matter the tense — only the main clause shows past.

exampleSentence.note: The default opening for an ongoing-action check-in.
N 중 is a concise status reply.

exampleSentence.en: I read a book while waiting.
exampleSentence.note: 동안 marks the overlapping time span.

exampleSentence.en: I am waiting for a friend.
exampleSentence.note: Waiting is a natural ongoing action.

exampleSentence.en: I am on a call right now.
I could not see the message during the meeting.
exampleSentence.note: A common reason for a delayed reply.

exampleSentence.en: I did not see the message.
exampleSentence.note: Often explained with an ongoing action.

exampleSentence.en: I am still in a meeting.
exampleSentence.note: 아직 pairs naturally with ongoing status.

exampleSentence.en: I am still studying / I keep studying.
I am resting for a moment.

exampleSentence.note: Natural quick reply to why you cannot talk.

exampleSentence.en: I am resting for a moment.

readingText.title: Why the reply was late
readingText.body: 지훈은 도서관에서 한국어를 공부하고 있었어요. 민서가 메시지를 보냈지만 지훈은 바로 답장하지 못했어요. 그때 지훈은 회의하는 동안 휴대폰을 보지 못했고, 회의가 끝난 뒤에도 발표 자료를 만드는 중이었어요. 민서는 카페에서 친구를 기다리는 중이라 시간이 조금 있었어요. 그래서 두 사람은 지훈이 끝나면 잠깐 전화하기로 했어요.
readingText.bodyTranslation: Jihoon was studying Korean at the library. Minseo sent a message, but Jihoon could not reply right away. During the meeting he could not check his phone, and after the meeting he was still making presentation materials. Minseo had a little time because she was waiting for a friend at a cafe, so they decided to call briefly when Jihoon finished.

comprehensionQuestions.question: 지훈은 왜 메시지를 바로 못 봤어요?

culturalNote.title: Short status replies
culturalNote.body: In Korean messaging, short status replies like 회의 중이에요, 가는 중이에요, and 지금 공부하고 있어요 are common and polite. They explain availability without over-explaining.
culturalNote.tip: Use N 중이에요 for quick status, and V-고 있어요 when you want to state the actual action.

inlineExercises.prompt: Which sentence describes an action in progress?
Which sentence is the best short status reply?
inlineExercises.explanation: N 중이에요 is a compact way to say an activity is in progress.

inlineExercises.prompt: During the meeting, I could not see the message.
inlineExercises.explanation: -는 동안 gives the time span during another action.
Use the verb modifier -는 before 중: 기다리는 중이에요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the sentence: 저는 바쁘고 있어요.
inlineExercises.explanation: Do not attach -고 있어요 to adjectives. Use a direct adjective or an action verb.

inlineExercises.prompt: 회의___ 하는 중이에요. (I am in the middle of a meeting.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 회의를 하다 is the action phrase “to have/do a meeting.” 회의를 하는 중이에요 means you are in the middle of that action.
-고 있어요 marks an action currently in progress. 공부하다 becomes 공부하고 있어요.

inlineExercises.prompt: Build: 'I am waiting for a friend now.' (Start with 지금.)
inlineExercises.explanation: 지금 sets the current moment. 기다리고 있어요 shows the waiting is happening now.
N 중이에요 is the compact way to say you are in the middle of a noun activity. 회의 중이에요 is a natural short status reply.

inlineExercises.prompt: Fix the sentence: '공부하고 동안 메시지를 못 봤어요.'
inlineExercises.explanation: 동안 needs the modifier form before it. 공부하다 becomes 공부하는 동안, not 공부하고 동안.

bullets: V-고 있어요 marks an action in progress: 한국어를 공부하고 있어요.
V-는 중이에요 and N 중이에요 focus on being in the middle of something: 회의 중이에요.
V-는 동안 marks an overlapping time span: 회의하는 동안 메시지를 못 봤어요.
Do not use -고 있어요 with adjectives like 바쁘다 or 피곤하다.

writingTask.prompt: Reply to a friend's message saying what you're doing right now and asking them to wait a moment.
writingTask.hint: Use V-고 있다 for an action in progress (공부하고 있어요), V-는 중이에요 for 'in the middle of' (회의 중이에요), and V-는 동안 for 'while' (기다리는 동안).
writingTask.model: 지금 회의하는 중이에요. 친구를 기다리는 동안 메시지를 보내요. 잠깐만요, 지금 일하고 있어요.
writingTask.modelEn: I'm in the middle of a meeting right now. I'm sending this message while waiting for a friend. Just a moment, I'm working right now.

canDo: Say an action is in progress with V-고 있다 (공부하고 있어요)
Say I'm in the middle of something with V-는 중이에요 (회의 중이에요)
Set one action against a stretch of time with V-는 동안 (기다리는 동안)
